questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac12$, $P(B)=\dfrac23$. Given that the events $A$ and $B$ are independent, find

(a) $P(A\cap B)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For independent events, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\times P(B)$:

$$P(A\cap B)=\frac12\times\frac23=\frac13.$$

**$P(A\cap B)=\dfrac13$.**

By the definition of conditional probability, $P(A'\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A'\cap B)}{P(B)}$.

$P(A'\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)=\dfrac23-\dfrac13=\dfrac13$.

$$P(A'\mid B)=\frac{1/3}{2/3}=\frac12.$$

(Quick check: if $A$ and $B$ are independent then so are $A'$ and $B$, so $P(A'\mid B)=P(A')=1-\frac12=\frac12$ ✓.)

**$P(A'\mid B)=\dfrac12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A bag contains $20$ balls, $5$ red and $15$ green. Two balls are drawn, at random from the bag, one after another without replacement.

(a) Draw a tree diagram to show all the possible outcomes. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first ball is red with probability $\dfrac5{20}=\dfrac14$ and green with probability $\dfrac{15}{20}=\dfrac34$. There is no replacement, so only $19$ balls remain for the second draw.

**Tree diagram** (R = red, G = green; probabilities on the branches):

- First ball **R** ($\frac14$)
  - Second ball **R** ($\frac4{19}$): outcome RR, probability $\frac14\times\frac4{19}=\frac1{19}$
  - Second ball **G** ($\frac{15}{19}$): outcome RG, probability $\frac14\times\frac{15}{19}=\frac{15}{76}$
- First ball **G** ($\frac34$)
  - Second ball **R** ($\frac5{19}$): outcome GR, probability $\frac34\times\frac5{19}=\frac{15}{76}$
  - Second ball **G** ($\frac{14}{19}$): outcome GG, probability $\frac34\times\frac{14}{19}=\frac{42}{76}=\frac{21}{38}$

Check: the two branches from each node add up to $1$ ($\frac4{19}+\frac{15}{19}=1$, $\frac5{19}+\frac{14}{19}=1$), and the four outcomes add up to $\frac4{76}+\frac{15}{76}+\frac{15}{76}+\frac{42}{76}=1$ ✓.
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Hence or otherwise, find the probability that the two balls are of different colours. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Different colours means "red then green" or "green then red" (mutually exclusive outcomes, so add):

$$P(\text{different})=P(RG)+P(GR)=\frac{15}{76}+\frac{15}{76}=\frac{30}{76}=\frac{15}{38}\approx0.395.$$

**The probability is $\dfrac{15}{38}$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) Hence or otherwise, find the probability that at least one ball is green. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The complement of "at least one green" is "no green", i.e. both balls red (RR):

$$P(\text{at least one green})=1-P(RR)=1-\frac1{19}=\frac{18}{19}\approx0.947.$$

(Check by adding the outcomes: $P(RG)+P(GR)+P(GG)=\frac{15}{76}+\frac{15}{76}+\frac{42}{76}=\frac{72}{76}=\frac{18}{19}$ ✓.)

**The probability is $\dfrac{18}{19}$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)
